key_insight: Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 switches polarization through a dynamic O3c/O4c oxygen-exchange pathway with transient bond formation, not just simple atomic displacement.
engineering_relevance: This microscopic mechanism explains HZO’s robust, low-strain switching behavior and points to preserving cooperative oxygen pathways as a design rule for durable, scalable non-volatile memories.
method: Electric-field-induced molecular dynamics on a defect-free ideal HZO lattice
Machine-learning force field (MACEField) tuned for the HZO system
Dynamic trajectory analysis of oxygen coordination changes and P–E hysteresis response
evidence_signal: The simulations reproduced the polarization–electric-field hysteresis loop and revealed coordinated oxygen exchange, transient detours, and internal self-compensation during switching.
watch_item: The results come from idealized defect-free simulations, so real-device defects, interfaces, and process variations may alter the switching pathway.
paper_title: Transient Detour and Cooperative Oxygen Exchange in the Polarization Switching of Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2
